name: ProcessManager
summary: Keeps the state of a multi-step process in one participant, so that a sequence with branches and joins can be decided as it goes rather than fixed when it starts.

roles.name: ProcessManager
roles.summary: The central participant that receives each reply and decides the next step. It is the alternative to a routing slip, and the trade is stated: it can branch on what the replies say, at the price of being a participant that holds state and can become a bottleneck.

roles.name: ProcessInstance
roles.summary: One running occurrence of the process, holding where it has got to. Separate from the manager because a manager serves many at once, and conflating them is how a process manager becomes a single-threaded one.

roles.name: ProcessTemplate
roles.summary: The definition the instances follow. It exists so that changing how a process runs is configuration rather than a class, which is the same knowledge-level move a posting rule makes for money.
